wikitext:
In manga, an {{wp|omnibus edition}} is a volume release collecting multiple volumes or arcs which were originally released separately. Manga publishers release omnibus collections typically of older works, combining them in a bargain format and often collecting a particular story arc, although some omnibus releases cover an entire manga series.

To date, the [[Pokémon Adventures]] manga has been released in omnibus format in several countries: in Japan, {{pmin|the United States}}/{{pmin|Canada}}/{{pmin|the United Kingdom}}/{{pmin|Australia}}, {{pmin|Singapore}}, {{pmin|France}}, {{pmin|Germany}}, {{pmin|Italy}}, {{pmin|Spain}}, and {{pmin|Vietnam}}.

==Japan==
===2011 releases===
In 2011, a series of omnibus releases were announced in Japan, collecting the {{MangaArc|Ruby & Sapphire}}. The arc was chosen due to its high popularity in Japan. These volumes were issued under [[Shogakukan]]'s "My First WIDE" brand.

While {{vol|My First Wide: Pocket Monsters Special Ruby Sapphire Chapter|1}} was released in March 2011, the other two planned volumes were cancelled and Volume 1 was quietly discontinued. This is believed to be due to the depictions of earthquakes and tsunami in the {{MangaArc|Ruby & Sapphire}}, which were deemed inappropriate following the {{wp|2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami}}.<ref>[http://pk-mn.com/n/pokemon-special-konbini-rs-my-first-big/ Pokémon Memo] (Japanese) (retrieved October 10, 2014)</ref>

===2014 releases===
In 2014, [[Shogakukan]] announced that they would be releasing a new omnibus edition of the {{MangaArc|Ruby & Sapphire}}, in commemoration of the release of [[Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire]]. The volumes were released under [[Shogakukan]]'s "My First BIG Special" brand, which are bargain-priced volumes sold only in Japanese convenience stores. A total of four volumes were released from October 24, 2014 to December 5, 2014.

[[Satoshi Yamamoto]] confirmed on his Twitter account that the new series of volumes has no connection to the 2011 releases and that the 2011 releases have been permanently discontinued.<ref>[https://twitter.com/satoshi_swalot/status/517440721674989569 Satoshi Yamamoto on Twitter] (Japanese)</ref>

===2017 releases===
In 2017, it was announced that a new omnibus edition of the {{MangaArc|Red, Green & Blue}} would be released under the title "Pocket Monsters Special Paperback Edition Red, Green & Blue Chapter". A total of two volumes were released, beginning with volume one on July 4. These volumes were later released in English in {{pmin|Singapore}} by [[Shogakukan Asia]] under the title "[[#Red, Green & Blue arc|Pokémon Adventures RGB]]".

==France==
===''Red, Green & Blue'' / ''Yellow'' arc===
On April 25, 2014, {{pmin|France|European French}} publisher Kurokawa announced they would start publishing the {{MangaArc2|Red, Green & Blue}} and {{MangaArc2|Yellow}} arcs together in omnibus format.<ref>[https://twitter.com/Kurokawa/status/459565765306228736 ''Pokémon - La Grande Aventure'' announcement - Twitter] (French)</ref> While both arcs had been previously released in France by publisher Glénat, these volumes feature a new translation. Kurokawa's omnibus volumes contain all the adventure route maps from the original Japanese volumes, but lack the character introduction pages from the beginning of those. A [[Manga boxed sets#France|boxed set]] containing the three volumes was released on November 9, 2017.<ref>[https://www.lisez.com/coffret/coffret-pokemon-la-grande-aventure-tomes-1-2-3-guide-pokemon/9782368525494 ''Pokémon - La Grande Aventure'' boxed set] (French)</ref>

==Spain==
In October 2015, {{pmin|Spain|Spanish}} publisher {{wp|Norma Editorial}} announced they would be publishing the entirety of the [[Pokémon Adventures]] manga. Due to the length of the series (52 volumes at the time of announcing the license) and due to different story arcs often starting and ending partway through volumes, Norma Editorial opted for an omnibus format, with 30 volumes released. The volumes have double numbering to accommodate fans who may wish to begin reading from a particular story arc. For example, the {{MangaArc|Yellow}} was published over two volumes, which were numbered as ''Yellow'' volumes 1 and 2, and as volumes 3 and 4 of the series overall.

The first volume to be released was {{tt|Pokémon Rojo, Verde y Azul|Pokémon Red, Green and Blue}} volume 1 on October 29, 2015. For their first releases, Norma Editorial alternated between the {{MangaArc2|Red, Green & Blue}} and {{MangaArc2|Black & White}} arcs. The {{MangaArc|Black 2 & White 2}} was eventually released in the same format as volumes 31 and 32.
